feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant public-sector impact. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited quantified outcomes beyond platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo is logical and supports the “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” positioning well.  
- Strong credibility: enterprise Drupal modernization, analytics stack expansion, studio buildout, and AI search work signal modern, high-value capability.  
- Good scope and relevance: combines strategy, governance, technical execution, analytics, and multimedia in a way that fits complex mission-driven organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears across multiple sections; consolidate Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT to avoid overlap.  
- Add more outcome metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include impact such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, campaign performance, or cost/time savings.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use consistent punctuation in lists, standardize “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” and keep serial comma usage consistent. Minor wording/style points: “A2/Learning” is awkward; use “A2 (learning).” “Ranked among the top public universities…” under Education feels unnecessary. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning that aligns well with the experience section, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and skills. Tightening it and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider a sharper version: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems. Builds and leads the governance, analytics, editorial, and multimedia systems that power mission-driven communications, including enterprise CMS modernization and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with “modernizing” or “leading” for stronger executive tone.
- Add a concrete scale marker if space allows, e.g., “10,000+ page websites” or “multi-million-page-view platforms.”
- Keep tense/style parallel: “Builds and leads…” reads more smoothly than shifting from “with experience building” to “Leads…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled content discovery” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and use parallel noun phrases for cleaner scanning.
- Emphasize higher-value leadership areas over operational detail already covered elsewhere.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization and CMS transformation • Digital governance, editorial systems, and publishing workflows • Analytics, dashboarding, and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications and campaign operations • AI-enabled search, discovery, and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder communications • Multimedia production, livestream, and studio operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled…experiences” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also covered in Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and foregrounding outcomes, platforms, or scope will make it more distinctive and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a clear deliverable and include one concrete differentiator (platform, audience, scale, or format).
- Replace vague wording like “improve discovery” and “designed for continued campaign growth” with sharper results-oriented language where possible.
- Suggested rewrite: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search — Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite — Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign — Produced a multi-part digital campaign spanning editorial features, archival media, web experiences, and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series — Launched a recurring advocacy video program covering editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely repeat achievements already covered in recent roles.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs if keeping this section.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 4–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.” Add usage, launch count, or audience metrics if available.
- Recast technical execution + AI search with impact: “Delivered CMS/front-end enhancements for high-traffic public sites and led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and user discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI-enabled search and microsite details duplicate the “Recent Projects” footer; keep this entry higher-level unless you add distinct outcomes.
- Governance/analytics language also overlaps with the NACo Director role; emphasize what is new/current here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more measurable where possible: add team size, budget, reporting cadence, production volume, engagement growth, cost savings, or turnaround improvements for email/social/video/analytics.
- Tighten weaker bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring video series”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-series language may duplicate both earlier NACo roles and Recent Projects.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national association audience.”
- Tighten bullets to emphasize ownership and outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show growth/innovation: “Launched and produced a recurring weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a consistent policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership verbs.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic digital/content phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, differentiated terms: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Content governance & editorial operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector advocacy communications,” “Audience strategy & content planning.”
- Consider adding scale where possible if format allows: e.g., “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing leadership concepts with execution wording.
- If space is tight, cut “audience-focused,” since audience orientation is implied by strategy/planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially duplicate the Core Competencies section.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles; keep only if this section needs sector specialization.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, higher-value capabilities and group tools under outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent/relevant platforms: keep Drupal first; consider dropping or de-emphasizing SharePoint/WordPress/Power Pages unless central to target roles.
- Tighten wording: change “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” to “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery).”
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search and discovery experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Most platform/tool names repeat in “Technical + IT”; Topline Skills should stay more strategic.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT, so this section should emphasize strategic application over software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating platforms here; move the full tool stack to Technical + IT.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • SEO, user behavior and performance analysis”
- If supported by results elsewhere, tie this skill area to impact language such as “decision-ready reporting” or “optimization insights for high-traffic public-sector platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure.”
- Tool list also overlaps almost exactly with “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent leadership-level delivery rather than generic task skills.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio and control-room operations,” “PTZ camera direction and switching.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio operations and PTZ camera systems • Virtual event production”
- If accurate, add scale or complexity instead of broad labels: e.g., “multi-camera livestream production” or “in-house studio production for advocacy and event programming.”
- Keep this as capability-focused; save tools/software detail for “Technical + IT.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” duplicate “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- “Video production and editing” overlaps with “Multimedia & Creative Tools”; avoid repeating execution-level detail unless you elevate it.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, high-value platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to a lower-priority item or remove it if usage was light.
- If space allows, add proficiency context: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want more impact, split by strength: **Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the Topline Skills entry listing the same platforms; keep one list broader and the other more selective.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same undifferentiated platform list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list rather than a senior, applied capability set. Tightening the phrasing and grouping tools by function would better match the leadership/implementation balance shown in recent roles.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from raw languages to applied execution: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers unless required: use “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3” for cleaner presentation.
- Consider adding scope/level if accurate: “working knowledge” or “implementation-level” to avoid implying deep software engineering if your experience is primarily web/platform delivery.
- If space allows, align to recent work: add “Drupal front-end implementation” or “CMS technical troubleshooting” since those appear in current/fresh roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- “API integrations” and automation themes overlap with Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so this item should stay tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Workflow Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add light context instead of just listing tools, e.g. “Used to build editorial workflows, intake systems, approvals, and cross-team coordination.”
- Consider dropping the weakest/oldest-use tools if not current; prioritize Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; listing all four may feel redundant unless each is genuinely current/relevant.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given the recent email leadership in NACo roles, but it’s currently just a vendor list. It would be stronger if framed around function and level of use, while staying concise and avoiding repeating channel leadership already covered in experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these are true hands-on tools; otherwise order by strongest/recentest platform.
- If space allows, add light context: **Email marketing, newsletter operations and audience engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- Put the most recent/enterprise-grade platform first; if Dynamics 365 was central in recent work, keep it leading.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters” or “tens of thousands of recipients” here; that impact is already covered well in Work Experience.
- If Higher Logic or Mailchimp were only legacy tools, consider dropping one to keep the section current.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently a generic list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize analysis/optimization capabilities rather than repeating platform names alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw tool list to a capability-led line: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity for analytics infrastructure, KPI reporting, user-behavior analysis, and optimization.”
- Replace vague terms like “Dashboarding” with stronger phrasing: “executive dashboards” or “leadership reporting.”
- Consider grouping by function for readability: “Analytics: GA4, BigQuery, Clarity • Reporting: Power BI, Looker Studio • Optimization: SEO, A/B testing.”
- If space allows, align wording with recent impact: “analytics infrastructure,” “performance analysis,” or “user-behavior insights,” which better supports the 2022–present roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one or making this version tools-only.
- “Dashboarding” overlaps with reporting language already implied by Power BI and Looker Studio.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving day-to-day operations across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 specific outputs or scale metrics: website refresh scope, number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, newsletter volume, or event coverage.
- Tighten the close: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”
- If space allows, split into two bullets for readability rather than one long paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical and foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest differentiator: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Add the standout accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten the multimedia line: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support research, member engagement, and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the first podcast launch.
- Avoid claiming broad digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent NACo roles already cover that progression.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production tools and avoid repeating broader multimedia themes already covered elsewhere.
